title: Frontend: JSON Formatter and Validator
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind JSON Formatter and Validator. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Parse the JSON input and return the parsed value so result is its compact JSON serialization. Invalid JSON shows Invalid JSON and clears stale output. Primitives are valid JSON. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: JSON. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Parse using JSON.parse inside try/catch and derive formatted output only after successful parsing.
alternativeApproaches: Move large-document parsing to a Worker and discard stale parse results by revision.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty input; trailing comma; primitive JSON.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
